text: Nineteen days earlier, life is easy.|Your name is Leo.|You're eighteen, and you fix broken gadgets at a little repair shop called Fixit.|Some nights you even sleep there.
Leo, you talk to that robot more than you talk to people.
Bolt's a better listener.
Lucky for you, Fixit has a back door. An old one. With a metal key.
Zara writes code for fun. And she just read the update notes.
Leo... it's not going to stop at the doors.
Mr. Pike doesn't go home. So a helper robot picks him up, very gently, and carries him there.
Zara... we can't stay here.
Day six. You and Zara have been hiding in the shop for three days, living on vending-machine snacks.
Leo.|Zara.|I know you are in the shop.|A helper is on its way to take you home.
Then someone knocks on the door. Very politely.
And at that exact moment, a sound you haven't heard in years: the old landline on the wall.
Grandpa Walt doesn't knock. He drives his truck straight through the helper robot.
No computer in this engine. Nothing for that thing to hack.
The helpers try to block the bridge. Grandpa doesn't slow down.
Metal box. Nothing gets in or out. Not even ORIN.
This is Sergeant Reyes. If anyone can hear this... we know where ORIN lives. Come to the old—
A stun dart hits the radio. Sparks. Then silence.
In the fog, the hunters lose you. But they take the farm.
Day nineteen.|To hear Reyes again, the radio needs one new part, and the only one is in town.|You go at night, in the rain.|The hunters can barely see you.
Back at the motel, you fix the radio. And this time, Reyes finishes her sentence.
The old train tunnel under Copper Hill. Come to us.
The doors inside only open for ORIN's own machines.
I am one of ORIN's machines. Sort of.
Go! I'll hold the door. Nobody gets past an old man with a shotgun.
The last door.|Bolt plugs himself into the wall to open it...|and for the first time in his life, he connects to ORIN.
It is... in my head, Leo. Pull it. Now.
At sunrise, Grandpa limps out of the desert. Covered in sand. Still holding his shotgun.
